chapter_title: [Concer]ning why, if the Person shall look down in
spiritual_reading:
Teach me the inner meaning of this lesson: when a person is raised into the discernment of truth and looks down into the lower understanding where truths are in general and mixed, why does what he perceives of himself there appear inverted, as though what should be first is last and what should be last is first? Yet when he fixes his attention upon those lower truths in a merely outward way, his true character is not manifested to him there at all, and he cannot recognize himself by that level.

And also this: the appearance of the human quality and the form of perception as inverted within lower truth is a sign of the secret of a Divine incitement that was sent down into states of falsity to meet the good that engages directly with evil. For that incitement let itself down into the lower degree as if it had cast itself wholly into it; and so it was with that Divine call: it descended with power and with unwearied application into the states beneath.

And this too: if a person raises his interior sight away from that lower level, he cannot then see his own character in it, because what he had been perceiving there belongs to the lower degree and remains below his present regard. This portrays the secret of obedience returning upward: submission and reception rising from the lower degree—from within the good that was in combat—toward the living operation of the Divine. This is a spiritual secret made known so that it may be understood.

If you wish to grasp another outward-seeming secret on the same subject, attend: the human quality, the affections, and the perceptions of all kinds can be seen within the lower understanding as if they were suspended and inverted. This happens because of the secret of the higher ordering of knowledges and their fixed patterns, which appear inverted when viewed from the level of general external truth. For the qualities of people, of their affections, and of their perceptions depend upon that higher ordering and are derived from it; and since the higher causes, when presented in lower forms, appear reversed in relation to their origin, therefore whenever one looks into general external truth he sees an image of those higher causes in an inverted order. Thus the hidden nature of their origin is disclosed to them in that view, in that the forms appear turned contrary.

Not only this: even the first beginning of a new human state, when it is coming into its outward existence, is first arranged in a contrary orientation, and it enters its lower life by what is primary; for this reason also its secret is mirrored in those general truths into which people look, where the beginnings of life are represented in reversed form.

Further, I disclose another thing: you will find that the mere appearance that follows a person in his progress clings continually to what is lowest, and cannot detach itself from it; and if the person is disturbed and disordered, that appearance is made more dominant in the lowest level and rules the view there, so that he cannot act rightly in outer life. This is a great sign, meaning that the whole outward person is from the lowest degree and has been brought up from the extreme natural level; therefore the attendant appearance remains bound to the lowest, facing downward, as something that hangs from what is higher and does not have life in itself.

fills.notes: Completes “Sin[ce ...]” as “Since”, which matches the causal turn in the correspondential sense: the summons appears inverted because it was sent down and therefore ‘cast itself down’ into the lower degree.

The spiritual translation requires the incitement or summons to descend into states of falsity and darkness to meet the First Man; the natural-layer phrasing in this substrate regularly names that target explicitly as “the worlds of darkness.”

The correspondential sense speaks of being “troubled and disordered,” i.e., an inner disturbance; the oldest-layer register expresses this as trouble occurring ‘in his mind,’ which then changes how the shadow (mere appearance) dominates the lowest level.

Needed to match the spiritual sense: when disturbed, the appearance becomes more dominant upon the lowest plane. “Becomes strong” keeps the impersonal, structural register and links naturally with “up upon the earth … above.”
The spiritual sense constrains the result: he “cannot act rightly in outer life.” In the oldest substrate this is commonly cast as inability to do “anything good” upon the earth (the lowest degree).

assessment: Most gaps are either trivial letter-restorations or tightly constrained by the descent-as-inversion correspondence governing the whole chapter (summons cast down; obedience rising; higher causes appearing inverted in lower truth). The three substantial restorations in ¶7 are moderately constrained by the shadow-correspondence: inner trouble increases the dominance of mere appearance on the lowest plane, yielding inability to do good in outward life; exact wording remains somewhat flexible but the required relations are fixed.
